standing.title: NYC Resistor Public Craft Night
standing.description: Open craft night at the NYC Resistor hacker collective: bring a project, use the space, meet members. Free and open to the public, 18 and over.
standing.time_note: Mondays and Thursdays 6:30-9:30pm. Free, but 18+ only.
standing.practical_note: Fourth-floor walkup; confirm on Eventbrite since craft night is occasionally cancelled for private classes.
standing.date_idea_reason: A free, hands-on makerspace evening is an unusual low-cost date with something to actually do.
standing.why_now: Runs twice a week year-round and is one of the few genuinely free weeknight drop-in activities.

standing.title: Whitney Museum free Friday evening
standing.description: The Whitney is free to all every Friday evening from 5 to 10pm, and also on the second Sunday of each month.
standing.time_note: Free admission Fridays 5-10pm. Free tickets are limited and released in advance.
standing.practical_note: Reserve the free timed ticket ahead; walk-up availability runs out on busy evenings.
standing.date_idea_reason: Free evening museum hours next to the High Line and a dense stretch of bars, so the museum is the anchor rather than the whole plan.
standing.why_now: A standing free window that makes a good anchor for a Friday evening in the Meatpacking District.

standing.title: Whitney Museum free second Sunday
standing.description: The Whitney offers free admission to everyone on the second Sunday of every month.
standing.time_note: Admission is free to all on the second Sunday of each month during normal hours.
standing.why_now: Falls in this window and only comes around once a month.

standing.title: MoMA free Friday evening
standing.description: MoMA offers free admission on Friday evenings. Free tickets are limited, released in advance, and go quickly.
standing.time_note: Free Friday evenings, roughly 4-8pm. Confirm the current window and ticket release on moma.org.
standing.practical_note: Book the free timed ticket the moment it is released; the line for walk-ups is long.
standing.why_now: A standing weekly free window at a museum that is otherwise one of the most expensive in the city.

holiday_plan.intro: Veterans Day falls on Wednesday, not a long weekend; confirm your own work schedule. These four options stay within roughly three hours' normal driving range of NYC, not a holiday-traffic guarantee. The overnight requires adding November 10 evening outside the stated one-day window. Beacon/Dia and Storm King were considered but replaced because their holiday access could not be verified.

trips.title: Cold Spring waterfront and Little Stony Point
trips.why: Combine village browsing and lunch with a Hudson shoreline walk, rather than committing to a strenuous summit hike.
trips.transport: Car-free: Metro-North Hudson Line from Grand Central to Cold Spring, then walking. Do not rely on the seasonal trolley: MTA lists weekend service only.
trips.time_budget: A full day including round-trip rail travel; finish park walking before sunset.
trips.booking_note: Check November 11 trains and service alerts in TrainTime. Hudson Highlands is open daily sunrise to sunset. Breakneck Ridge trailhead and its station are closed for the construction project; use official maps to select open routes. Confirm individual restaurant hours.

trips.title: Hudson and Olana's artist-designed landscape
trips.why: Explore Frederic Church's landscape composition and exterior architecture during his bicentenary year, followed by a meal in Hudson. This is an outdoor art-and-landscape outing, not a house-tour recommendation.
trips.transport: Car-required for this itinerary. Olana recommends a personal car because local taxi and rideshare service is limited; do not assume an effortless connection from Hudson station.
trips.time_budget: A long day trip. Olana estimates 2.5 hours driving from NYC each way, before traffic and stops.
trips.booking_note: Olana's grounds are free and open daily, 8 a.m. to sunset according to its own visitor page. The house is closed November 2–19 for exhibition installation, and landscape tours in that period run only Saturday–Sunday. Do not expect Wednesday tours or an indoor visitor-center stop. Confirm Hudson dining hours separately.

trips.title: Philadelphia history and market-food overnight
trips.why: Pair Independence Hall and the Liberty Bell with Reading Terminal Market during the nation's 250th anniversary year. Staying the preceding night gives November 11 more room for history and food.
trips.transport: Car-free: Amtrak from New York Penn Station to Philadelphia 30th Street, then SEPTA and walking. Exact trains, fares and holiday service remain unconfirmed.
trips.time_budget: Optional November 10 evening arrival, one night, and November 11 return. This extends beyond the one-day window; use a same-day version if that extension is unavailable.
trips.booking_note: Check a cancellable hotel and round-trip trains before committing; no availability was verified. NPS lists Independence Hall's November open house at 9–10:30 a.m., followed by ticketed tours from 10:40 a.m.; allow time for security. Reading Terminal Market lists daily 8 a.m.–6 p.m. hours, with merchant variations and no November 11 closure on its 2026 list. The Philadelphia Museum of Art is closed Wednesdays, so it is not part of this itinerary.

trips.title: Caumsett's coastal estate landscape
trips.why: A nature-focused alternative: walk through former estate grounds, woodland and meadows toward Long Island Sound, with routes chosen from the official trail map.
trips.transport: Car-required for this itinerary: drive to the public visitor parking at Caumsett, 25 Lloyd Harbor Road. This is not presented as a station-to-trail car-free outing.
trips.time_budget: An unhurried day trip with a substantial daylight walking block and a return before or after dinner.
trips.booking_note: The park lists year-round daily opening from sunrise to sunset. Bring food and water: the cafe's published season ends in October. Pets are prohibited. Use ordinary visitor parking, not the permit-restricted fishing road or parking area; check current alerts and any applicable vehicle fee.

local_ideas.title: NYC Veterans Day Parade
local_ideas.why: The organizer confirms the Fifth Avenue parade, with astronaut and Navy veteran Sunita Williams as 2026 grand marshal. Check the final spectator route, start time and street restrictions; those details were not established by the retrieved page.

local_ideas.title: Intrepid Museum and Veterans Day ceremony
local_ideas.why: Combine naval and aviation history with the confirmed 3:30–4:30 p.m. ceremony in Hangar 3 and commemorative wreath laying. The ceremony is included with museum admission, not a promise of free museum entry. Published museum hours are 10 a.m.–5 p.m., last entry 4 p.m.; check timed admission. A livestream is also announced.

items.title: The Dynamo Room: $35.95 express lunch and daily happy hour
items.address: 2 Pennsylvania Plaza, New York, NY 10121; entrance on West 33rd Street between Seventh and Eighth Avenues
items.summary: The express lunch includes Parker House rolls, a salad choice, and spaghetti pomodoro or salmon. Happy hour offers oysters and smaller-format cocktails near Penn Station.

items.schedule: Lunch Monday–Thursday 11:30am–2:30pm. Happy hour daily 4–6pm.

items.conditions: Wine flights become $19 after 6pm. Wine-of-the-day selections vary. No oyster minimum or mandatory beverage purchase is stated. Reservation requirement, tax, gratuity and service charges for happy hour are not stated.
items.verification_note: Checked the current restaurant-owned menu and location page. Used its $26 early-bird price rather than the older $21 editorial figure. Holiday exceptions were not established.
